title: Ghostwriter settings cannot be reached for first-time setup
reasoning: The only navigation entry to GhostwriterSettingsView is hidden unless Ghostwriter is already enabled or the hard-coded feature flag is true. Because the feature flag is false and new installs default to ghostwriterEnabled=false, users cannot reach the screen that contains the enable toggle, server URL, and API token setup. Existing configured users may still see it, but first-time configuration is blocked.
reproduction: On a fresh install with no ghostwriter_enabled UserDefaults value, open Settings. The Ghostwriter section is not rendered, so there is no path to the Ghostwriter configuration screen.
recommendation: Render the Ghostwriter navigation row whenever the feature is available, regardless of the current enabled state, or move the enable/server/token controls into SettingsView before gating runtime-only sync actions.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: App/Tests/EpilogueTests.swift only contains a placeholder assertion, and SettingsRepositoryTests exercise persistence methods but not SettingsView routing or first-time setup visibility.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SwiftUI/view-model test or snapshot that starts with isGhostwriterEnabled=false and asserts that SettingsView still exposes a Ghostwriter settings entry point.
minimumFixScope: App/Sources/Views/SettingsView.swift conditional rendering for the Ghostwriter settings section.

history.reasoning: The original evidence path still exists, but the blocking condition has changed. App/Sources/Views/SettingsView.swift no longer has `private let ghostwriterSettingsEnabled = false`; it now has `private static let ghostwriterSettingsAvailable = true` and `shouldShowGhostwriterSettings(ghostwriterEnabled:)` returns true when Ghostwriter is disabled. The Ghostwriter section condition now calls that helper, so the NavigationLink to GhostwriterSettingsView is rendered for first-time setup. App/Sources/Views/GhostwriterSettingsView.swift still contains the enable toggle at lines 29-32. There is also a regression test in App/Tests/EpilogueTests.swift asserting `SettingsView.shouldShowGhostwriterSettings(ghostwriterEnabled: false)`. I attempted to run tests with xcodebuildmcp, but execution was blocked by the read-only sandbox/temp-directory EPERM and the generated workspace was not present; the current source and added test source nevertheless directly address the reported reachability bug.
